column11: TIVDAK WAC 7,400.80 USD per 40 mg single-dose vial, from Pfizer's own statutory price disclosure short form (Connecticut HB 6669, data as of 28-Jul-2025, cdn.pfizer.com/pfizercom/products/ctprescribers/TIVDAKCTPriceDisclosureShortForm07282025.pdf). The label's recommended dose is 2 mg/kg, up to a maximum of 200 mg, by intravenous infusion every 3 weeks until progression. Mean body weight for US women aged 20 and over is 77.9 kg on CDC NHANES August 2021 to August 2023, so 2 mg/kg is 155.8 mg, which takes four 40 mg vials (160 mg) with no vial sharing: 4 x 7,400.80 = 29,603.20 USD a cycle. 365/21 = 17.381 cycles a year: 29,603.20 x 365/21 = 514,531.81 USD a year
column12: the annual rate for a patient who stays on it a full year. With a median progression-free survival of 4.2 months almost nobody does, which is what the discontinuation row carries. Weight is taken on women because the approved population is cervical cancer; the solid-tumour cohorts here are mixed-sex and would run slightly higher

column11: reused from the Medicare Part B average sales price convention the book applies to physician-administered drugs elsewhere, 5.66% below list. column12: shallow by design. Part B drugs are reimbursed at ASP plus 6% and carry no Part D style formulary rebate, so the gap between list and net is small

column11: derived from innovaTV 301 (ENGOT-cx12/GOG-3057), the Phase 3 that registered tisotumab vedotin: median progression-free survival 4.2 months (95% CI 4.0 to 4.4) against 2.9 months with chemotherapy, and median overall survival 11.5 months against 9.5 (Vergote I et al., Tisotumab vedotin as second- or third-line therapy for recurrent cervical cancer, New England Journal of Medicine 2024, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2313811). At a constant hazard the annual stopping rate is 1 - exp(-ln2 / (4.2/12)) = 1 - exp(-1.98042) = 0.8620
column12: very high, and correctly so: this is a late-line antibody-drug conjugate in an aggressive tumour, and the stock empties within a year
